  * ### Method Detail

    * #### execute

      ```
      public ClassicHttpResponse execute(ClassicHttpRequest request,
                                         ExecChain.Scope scope,
                                         ExecChain chain)
                                  throws IOException,
                                         HttpException
      ```

      Description copied from interface: `ExecChainHandler`

      Executes the actual HTTP request. The handler can choose to return
      a response message or delegate request execution to the next element
      in the execution chain.

      Specified by:
      :   `execute` in interface `ExecChainHandler`

      Parameters:
      :   `request` - the actual request.
      :   `scope` - the execution scope .
      :   `chain` - the next element in the request execution chain.

      Throws:
      :   `IOException`
      :   `HttpException`

* * [org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio.support.BasicRequestProducer](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/support/BasicRequestProducer.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio.support")
  * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods.SimpleRequestProducer

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [AsyncDataProducer](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/AsyncDataProducer.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio"), [AsyncRequestProducer](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/AsyncRequestProducer.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio"), [ResourceHolder](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/ResourceHolder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio")

  ---

    

  ```
  public final class SimpleRequestProducer
  extends BasicRequestProducer
  ```

  HTTP request producer that generates message data stream events based
  on content of a [`SimpleHttpRequest`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/async/methods/SimpleHttpRequest.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods") instance.

  IMPORTANT: [`SimpleHttpRequest`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/async/methods/SimpleHttpRequest.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods")s are intended for simple scenarios where entities inclosed
  in requests are known to be small. It is generally recommended to use
  [`AsyncRequestBuilder`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/support/AsyncRequestBuilder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio.support") and streaming
  [`AsyncEntityProducer`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/AsyncEntityProducer.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio")s.

  Since:
  :   5.0

  See Also:
  :   [`SimpleBody`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/async/methods/SimpleBody.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods"),
      [`SimpleHttpRequest`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/async/methods/SimpleHttpRequest.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods"),
      [`AsyncRequestBuilder`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/support/AsyncRequestBuilder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio.support"),
      [`AsyncEntityProducer`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/AsyncEntityProducer.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio")

      * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods.SimpleHttpRequest

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.io"), [Configurable](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/config/Configurable.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.config"), [HttpMessage](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/HttpMessage.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http"), [HttpRequest](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/HttpRequest.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http"), [MessageHeaders](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/MessageHeaders.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http")

  ---

    

  ```
  public final class SimpleHttpRequest
  extends ConfigurableHttpRequest
  ```

  HTTP request that can enclose a body represented as a simple text string or an array of bytes.

  IMPORTANT: [`SimpleHttpRequest`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/async/methods/SimpleHttpRequest.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods")s are intended for simple scenarios where entities inclosed
  in requests are known to be small. It is generally recommended to use
  [`AsyncRequestBuilder`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/support/AsyncRequestBuilder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio.support") and streaming
  [`AsyncEntityProducer`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/AsyncEntityProducer.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio")s.

  Since:
  :   5.0

  See Also:
  :   [`SimpleBody`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/async/methods/SimpleBody.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods"),
      [`AsyncRequestBuilder`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/support/AsyncRequestBuilder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio.support"),
      [`AsyncEntityProducer`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/AsyncEntityProducer.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio"),

## Enum ContentCoding

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * [java.lang.Enum](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Enum.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")<[ContentCoding](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/entity/compress/ContentCoding.html "enum in org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity.compress")>
  * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity.compress.ContentCoding

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.io"), [Comparable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Comparable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")<[ContentCoding](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/entity/compress/ContentCoding.html "enum in org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity.compress")>

  ---

    

  ```
  public enum ContentCoding
  extends Enum<ContentCoding>
  ```

  Enumeration of the canonical IANA content-coding tokens supported by HttpClient for
  HTTP request and response bodies.

  Each constant corresponds to the standard token used in the `Content-Encoding`
  and `Accept-Encoding` headers. Some codings (e.g. Brotli, Zstandard, XZ/LZMA)
  may require additional helper libraries at runtime.

  Since:
  :   5.6

* * ### Enum Constant Summary

    Enum Constants

    | Enum Constant and Description |
    | `BROTLI` Brotli compression format. |
    | `BZIP2` BZIP2 compression format. |
    | `DEFLATE` "deflate" compression format (zlib or raw). |
    | `DEFLATE64` Deflate64 compression format. |
    | `GZIP` GZIP compression format. |
    | `LZ4_BLOCK` Block LZ4 compression format. |
    | `LZ4_FRAMED` Framed LZ4 compression format. |
    | `LZMA` LZMA compression format. |
    | `PACK200` Pack200 compression format. |
    | `X_GZIP` Legacy alias for GZIP. |
    | `XZ` XZ compression format. |
    | `ZSTD` Zstandard compression format. |

      Lookup an enum by its token (case‐insensitive), or `null` if none matches.

## Class CookiePathComparator

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie.CookiePathComparator

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.io"), [Comparator](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Comparator.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.util")<[Cookie](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/Cookie.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie")>

  ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=STATELESS)
  public class CookiePathComparator
  extends Object
  implements Serializable, Comparator<Cookie>
  ```

  This cookie comparator ensures that multiple cookies satisfying
  a common criteria are ordered in the [`Cookie`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/Cookie.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie") header such
  that those with more specific Path attributes precede those with
  less specific.

  This comparator assumes that Path attributes of two cookies
  path-match a common request-URI. Otherwise, the result of the
  comparison is undefined.

  Since:
  :   4.0

  See Also:
  :   [Serialized Form](../../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie.CookiePathComparator)

## Class BasicHttpClientResponseHandler

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * [org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.AbstractHttpClientResponseHandler](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/AbstractHttpClientResponseHandler.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic")<[String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")>
  * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.BasicHttpClientResponseHandler

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [HttpClientResponseHandler](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/io/HttpClientResponseHandler.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.io")<[String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")>

  ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=STATELESS)
  public class BasicHttpClientResponseHandler
  extends AbstractHttpClientResponseHandler<String>
  ```

  A [`HttpClientResponseHandler`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/io/HttpClientResponseHandler.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.io") that returns
  the response body as a String for successful (2xx) responses. If the response
  code was >= 300, the response body is consumed
  and an [`HttpResponseException`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/HttpResponseException.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http") is thrown.

  If this is used with
  [`HttpClient.execute(
  org.apache.hc.core5.http.ClassicHttpRequest,
  org.apache.hc.core5.http.io.HttpClientResponseHandler)`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/classic/HttpClient.html#execute-org.apache.hc.core5.http.ClassicHttpRequest-org.apache.hc.core5.http.io.HttpClientResponseHandler-),
  HttpClient may handle redirects (3xx responses) internally.

  Since:
  :   4.0

    * #### DefaultHttpRequestRetryStrategy

      ```
      public DefaultHttpRequestRetryStrategy(int maxRetries,
                                             TimeValue defaultRetryInterval)
      ```

      Create the HTTP request retry strategy using the following list of
      non-retriable I/O exception classes:  
      * InterruptedIOException
      * UnknownHostException
      * ConnectException
      * ConnectionClosedException
      * NoRouteToHostException
      * SSLExceptionand retriable HTTP status codes:  
      * SC\_TOO\_MANY\_REQUESTS (429)
      * SC\_SERVICE\_UNAVAILABLE (503)

      Parameters:
      :   `maxRetries` - how many times to retry; 0 means no retries
      :   `defaultRetryInterval` - the default retry interval between
          subsequent retries if the `Retry-After` header is not set
          or invalid.
    * #### DefaultHttpRequestRetryStrategy

      ```
      public DefaultHttpRequestRetryStrategy()
      ```

      Create the HTTP request retry strategy with a max retry count of 1,
      default retry interval of 1 second, and using the following list of
      non-retriable I/O exception classes:  
      * InterruptedIOException
      * UnknownHostException
      * ConnectException
      * ConnectionClosedException
      * SSLExceptionand retriable HTTP status codes:  
      * SC\_TOO\_MANY\_REQUESTS (429)
      * SC\_SERVICE\_UNAVAILABLE (503)

    * #### parse

      ```
      public final List<Cookie> parse(Header header,
                                      CookieOrigin origin)
                               throws MalformedCookieException
      ```

      Description copied from interface: `CookieSpec`

      Parse the `"Set-Cookie"` Header into an array of Cookies.

      This method will not perform the validation of the resultant
      [`Cookie`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/Cookie.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie")s

      Specified by:
      :   `parse` in interface `CookieSpec`

      Parameters:
      :   `header` - the `Set-Cookie` received from the server
      :   `origin` - details of the cookie origin

      Returns:
      :   an array of `Cookie`s parsed from the header

      Throws:
      :   `MalformedCookieException` - if an exception occurs during parsing

      See Also:
      :   [`CookieSpec.validate(org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie.Cookie, org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie.CookieOrigin)`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/CookieSpec.html#validate-org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie.Cookie-org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie.CookieOrigin-)

    * #### parse

      ```
      public PublicSuffixList parse(Reader reader)
                             throws IOException
      ```

      Parses the public suffix list format.

      When creating the reader from the file, make sure to use the correct encoding
      (the original list is in UTF-8).

      Parameters:
      :   `reader` - the data reader. The caller is responsible for closing the reader.

      Throws:
      :   `IOException` - on error while reading from list
    * #### parseByType

      ```
      public List<PublicSuffixList> parseByType(Reader reader)
                                         throws IOException
      ```

      Parses the public suffix list format by domain type (currently supported ICANN and PRIVATE).

      When creating the reader from the file, make sure to use the correct encoding
      (the original list is in UTF-8).

      Parameters:
      :   `reader` - the data reader. The caller is responsible for closing the reader.

      Throws:
      :   `IOException` - on error while reading from list

      Since:
      :   4.5

* * ### Method Detail

    * #### setExpectContinueEnabled

      ```
      public RequestConfig.Builder setExpectContinueEnabled(boolean expectContinueEnabled)
      ```

      Determines whether the 'Expect: 100-Continue' handshake is enabled
      for entity enclosing methods. The purpose of the 'Expect: 100-Continue'
      handshake is to allow a client that is sending a request message with
      a request body to determine if the origin server is willing to
      accept the request (based on the request headers) before the client
      sends the request body.

      The use of the 'Expect: 100-continue' handshake can result in
      a noticeable performance improvement for entity enclosing requests
      (such as POST and PUT) that require the target server's
      authentication.

      'Expect: 100-continue' handshake should be used with caution, as it
      may cause problems with HTTP servers and proxies that do not support
      HTTP/1.1 protocol.

      Default: `false`

      Returns:
      :   this instance.

    * #### setResponseTimeout

      ```
      public RequestConfig.Builder setResponseTimeout(Timeout responseTimeout)
      ```

      Determines the timeout until arrival of a response from the opposite
      endpoint.

      A timeout value of zero is interpreted as an infinite timeout.

      Please note that response timeout may be unsupported by
      HTTP transports with message multiplexing.

      This parameter overrides the socket timeout setting applied at the connection
      management or I/O layers for the duration of a message exchange.

      Please note that response timeout is not a deadline. Its absolute value
      can be exceeded, for example, in case of automatic request re-execution.
      Please make sure the automatic request re-execution policy has been
      configured appropriately.

      Default: `null`

      Returns:
      :   this instance.

      Since:
      :   5.0

    * #### setHardCancellationEnabled

      ```
      public RequestConfig.Builder setHardCancellationEnabled(boolean hardCancellationEnabled)
      ```

      Determines whether request cancellation, such as through `Future#cancel(boolean)`, should kill the underlying connection. If this
      option is set to false, the client will attempt to preserve the
      underlying connection by allowing the request to complete in the
      background, discarding the response.

      Note that when this option is `true`, cancelling a request may
      cause other requests to fail, if they are waiting to use the same
      connection.

      On HTTP/2, this option has no effect. Request cancellation will always
      result in the stream being cancelled with a `RST_STREAM`. This
      has no effect on connection reuse.

      On non-asynchronous clients, this option has no effect. Request
      cancellation, such as through `HttpUriRequestBase#cancel()`, will
      always kill the underlying connection.

      Default: `true`

      Returns:
      :   this instance.

      Since:
      :   5.0

    * #### rewriteURI

      ```
      @Deprecated
      public static URI rewriteURI(URI uri,
                                                HttpHost target,
                                                boolean dropFragment)
                                         throws URISyntaxException
      ```

      Deprecated. Use [`URIBuilder`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/net/URIBuilder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.net").

      A convenience method for creating a new [`URI`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URI.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.net") whose scheme, host
      and port are taken from the target host, but whose path, query and
      fragment are taken from the existing URI. The fragment is only used if
      dropFragment is false. The path is set to "/" if not explicitly specified.

      Parameters:
      :   `uri` - Contains the path, query and fragment to use.
      :   `target` - Contains the scheme, host and port to use.
      :   `dropFragment` - True if the fragment should not be copied.

      Throws:
      :   `URISyntaxException` - If the resulting URI is invalid.

    * #### rewriteURI

      ```
      @Deprecated
      public static URI rewriteURI(URI uri)
                                         throws URISyntaxException
      ```

      Deprecated. Use [`URIBuilder`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/net/URIBuilder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.net").

      A convenience method that creates a new [`URI`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URI.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.net") whose scheme, host, port, path,
      query are taken from the existing URI, dropping any fragment or user-information.
      The path is set to "/" if not explicitly specified. The existing URI is returned
      unmodified if it has no fragment or user-information and has a path.

      Parameters:
      :   `uri` - original URI.

      Throws:
      :   `URISyntaxException` - If the resulting URI is invalid.

    * #### resolve

      ```
      public static URI resolve(URI originalURI,
                                HttpHost target,
                                List<URI> redirects)
                         throws URISyntaxException
      ```

      Derives the interpreted (absolute) URI that was used to generate the last
      request. This is done by extracting the request-uri and target origin for
      the last request and scanning all the redirect locations for the last
      fragment identifier, then combining the result into a [`URI`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URI.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.net").

      Parameters:
      :   `originalURI` - original request before any redirects
      :   `target` - if the last URI is relative, it is resolved against this target,
          or `null` if not available.
      :   `redirects` - collection of redirect locations since the original request
          or `null` if not available.

      Returns:
      :   interpreted (absolute) URI

      Throws:
      :   `URISyntaxException`

  :   [Cookie](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/Cookie.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie")

  All Known Implementing Classes:
  :   [BasicClientCookie](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/cookie/BasicClientCookie.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.cookie")

  ---

    

  ```
  public interface SetCookie
  extends Cookie
  ```

  This interface represents a `Set-Cookie` response header sent by the
  origin server to the HTTP agent in order to maintain a conversational state.

  Since:
  :   4.0

      ```
      @Deprecated

      ```

      Deprecated. Use {[`setExpiryDate(Instant)`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/SetCookie.html#setExpiryDate-java.time.Instant-)}

      Sets expiration date.

      **Note:** the object returned by this method is considered
      immutable. Changing it (e.g. using setTime()) could result in undefined
      behaviour. Do so at your peril.

      Parameters:
      :   `expiryDate` - the [`Date`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.util") after which this cookie is no longer valid.

      Sets expiration date.

      **Note:** the object returned by this method is considered

      your peril.

      Parameters:

    * #### setSecure

      ```
      void setSecure(boolean secure)
      ```

      Sets the secure attribute of the cookie.

      When `true` the cookie should only be sent
      using a secure protocol (https). This should only be set when
      the cookie's originating server used a secure protocol to set the
      cookie's value.

      Parameters:
      :   `secure` - The value of the secure attribute

      See Also:
      :   [`Cookie.isSecure()`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/Cookie.html#isSecure--)

## Class MinimalHttpClient

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * [org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.CloseableHttpClient](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/CloseableHttpClient.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic")
  * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.MinimalHttpClient

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.io"), [AutoCloseable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/AutoCloseable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang"), [HttpClient](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/classic/HttpClient.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.classic"), [ModalCloseable](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/io/ModalCloseable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.io")

  ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=SAFE_CONDITIONAL)
  public class MinimalHttpClient
  extends CloseableHttpClient
  ```

  Minimal implementation of [`CloseableHttpClient`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/CloseableHttpClient.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic"). This client is
  optimized for HTTP/1.1 message transport and does not support advanced
  HTTP protocol functionality such as request execution via a proxy, state
  management, authentication and request redirects.

  Concurrent message exchanges executed by this client will get assigned to
  separate connections leased from the connection pool.

  Since:
  :   4.3

## Class AbstractHttpClientResponseHandler<T>

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.AbstractHttpClientResponseHandler<T>

* Type Parameters:
  :   `T` - the type of the value determined by the response.

  All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [HttpClientResponseHandler](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/io/HttpClientResponseHandler.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.io")<T>

  Direct Known Subclasses:
  :   [BasicHttpClientResponseHandler](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/BasicHttpClientResponseHandler.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic")

  ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=STATELESS)
  public abstract class AbstractHttpClientResponseHandler<T>
  extends Object
  implements HttpClientResponseHandler<T>
  ```

  A generic [`HttpClientResponseHandler`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/io/HttpClientResponseHandler.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.io") that works with the response entity
  for successful (2xx) responses. If the response code was >= 300, the response
  body is consumed and an [`HttpResponseException`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/HttpResponseException.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http") is thrown.

  If this is used with
  [`HttpClient.execute(
  org.apache.hc.core5.http.ClassicHttpRequest, HttpClientResponseHandler)`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/classic/HttpClient.html#execute-org.apache.hc.core5.http.ClassicHttpRequest-org.apache.hc.core5.http.io.HttpClientResponseHandler-),
  HttpClient may handle redirects (3xx responses) internally.

  Since:
  :   4.4

    | `AbstractHttpClientResponseHandler()` |

      ```
      public T handleResponse(ClassicHttpResponse response)
                       throws IOException
      ```

      Read the entity from the response body and pass it to the entity handler
      method if the response was successful (a 2xx status code). If no response
      body exists, this returns null. If the response was unsuccessful (>= 300
      status code), throws an [`HttpResponseException`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/HttpResponseException.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http").

      Specified by:

## Class ScramException

        * * [org.apache.hc.client5.http.auth.AuthenticationException](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/auth/AuthenticationException.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.auth")
          * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.ScramException

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.io")

  ---

    

  ```
  public class ScramException
  extends AuthenticationException
  ```

  Represents an exception that occurs during SCRAM (Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism) authentication.

  SCRAM is a family of SASL mechanisms used for secure authentication. This exception is thrown when
  an error or issue is encountered during the SCRAM authentication process.

  Since:
  :   5.6

  See Also:
  :   [Serialized Form](../../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.ScramException)

## Class AIMDBackoffManager

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * [org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.AbstractBackoff](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/AbstractBackoff.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic")
  * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.AIMDBackoffManager

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [BackoffManager](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/classic/BackoffManager.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.classic")

  ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=SAFE)
  public class AIMDBackoffManager
  extends AbstractBackoff
  ```

  The `AIMDBackoffManager` applies an additive increase,
  multiplicative decrease (AIMD) to managing a dynamic limit to
  the number of connections allowed to a given host. You may want
  to experiment with the settings for the cooldown periods and the
  backoff factor to get the adaptive behavior you want.

  Generally speaking, shorter cooldowns will lead to more steady-state
  variability but faster reaction times, while longer cooldowns
  will lead to more stable equilibrium behavior but slower reaction
  times.

  Similarly, higher backoff factors promote greater
  utilization of available capacity at the expense of fairness
  among clients. Lower backoff factors allow equal distribution of
  capacity among clients (fairness) to happen faster, at the
  expense of having more server capacity unused in the short term.

  Since:
  :   4.2

* * ### Constructor Summary

    | `void` | `setBackoffFactor(double d)` Sets the factor to use when backing off; the new per-host limit will be roughly the current max times this factor. |

* * ### Constructor Detail

    * #### AIMDBackoffManager

      ```
      public AIMDBackoffManager(ConnPoolControl<HttpRoute> connPerRoute)
      ```

      Constructs an `AIMDBackoffManager` with the specified
      [`ConnPoolControl`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/pool/ConnPoolControl.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.pool") and `Clock`.

      This constructor is primarily used for testing purposes, allowing the
      injection of a custom `Clock` implementation.

      Parameters:
      :   `connPerRoute` - the [`ConnPoolControl`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/pool/ConnPoolControl.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.pool") that manages
          per-host routing maximums
  * ### Method Detail

    * #### getBackedOffPoolSize

      ```
      protected int getBackedOffPoolSize(int curr)
      ```

      Returns the backed-off pool size based on the current pool size.
      The new pool size is calculated as the floor of (backoffFactor \* curr).

      Specified by:
      :   `getBackedOffPoolSize` in class `AbstractBackoff`

      Parameters:
      :   `curr` - the current pool size

      Returns:
      :   the backed-off pool size, with a minimum value of 1
    * #### setBackoffFactor

      ```
      public void setBackoffFactor(double d)
      ```

      Sets the factor to use when backing off; the new
      per-host limit will be roughly the current max times
      this factor. `Math.floor` is applied in the
      case of non-integer outcomes to ensure we actually
      decrease the pool size. Pool sizes are never decreased
      below 1, however. Defaults to 0.5.

      Parameters:
      :   `d` - must be between 0.0 and 1.0, exclusive.

      public void addCookie(Cookie cookie)

      Adds an [`HTTP cookie`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/Cookie.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie"), replacing any existing equivalent cookies.
      If the given cookie has already expired it will not be added, but existing
      values will still be removed.

      Specified by:
      :   `addCookie` in interface `CookieStore`

      Parameters:

    * #### addCookies

      ```

      Adds an array of [`HTTP cookies`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/Cookie.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie"). Cookies are added individually and
      in the given array order. If any of the given cookies has already expired it will
      not be added, but existing values will still be removed.

## Class DeflatingAsyncEntityProducer

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods.DeflatingAsyncEntityProducer

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [EntityDetails](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/EntityDetails.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http"), [AsyncDataProducer](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/AsyncDataProducer.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio"), [AsyncEntityProducer](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/AsyncEntityProducer.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio"), [ResourceHolder](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/nio/ResourceHolder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.nio")

  ---

    

  ```
  public final class DeflatingAsyncEntityProducer
  extends Object
  implements AsyncEntityProducer
  ```

  `AsyncEntityProducer` that streams the output of another producer
  through the raw DEFLATE compression algorithm.

  The delegate’s bytes are read in small chunks, compressed with
  [`Deflater`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/Deflater.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.util.zip") and written immediately to the HTTP I/O
  layer. Memory use is therefore bounded even for very large request
  entities.

  Since:
  :   5.6

* * ### Enum Constant Detail

    * #### LEGACY

      ```
      public static final HttpMultipartMode LEGACY
      ```

      Legacy compatibility mode.

      In this mode only the most essential fields are generated
      such as Content-Type and Content-Disposition.
    * #### STRICT

      ```
      public static final HttpMultipartMode STRICT
      ```

      Strict MIME specification conformance.

      Presently conforms to RFC 822, RFC 2045, RFC 2046.
    * #### EXTENDED

      ```
      public static final HttpMultipartMode EXTENDED
      ```

      Extended MIME specification conformance.

      In this mode header field values may contain international UTF-8 encoded
      characters.

      Presently conforms to RFC 6532 and RFC 7578.

## Class ConnectExec

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")

  :   [ExecChainHandler](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/classic/ExecChainHandler.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.classic")

  ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=STATELESS)
   @Internal
  public final class ConnectExec
  extends Object
  implements ExecChainHandler
  ```

  Request execution handler in the classic request execution chain
  that is responsible for establishing connection to the target
  origin server as specified by the current connection route.

  Since:
  :   5.0

* * ### Constructor Summary

  * ### Method Detail

    * #### execute

      ```
      public ClassicHttpResponse execute(ClassicHttpRequest request,
                                         ExecChain.Scope scope,
                                         ExecChain chain)
                                  throws IOException,
                                         HttpException
      ```

      Description copied from interface: `ExecChainHandler`

      Executes the actual HTTP request. The handler can choose to return
      a response message or delegate request execution to the next element
      in the execution chain.

      Specified by:
      :   `execute` in interface `ExecChainHandler`

      Parameters:
      :   `request` - the actual request.
      :   `scope` - the execution scope .
      :   `chain` - the next element in the request execution chain.

      Throws:
      :   `IOException`
      :   `HttpException`

* * ### Method Detail

    * #### getMimeType

      ```
      String getMimeType()
      ```

      Returns the body descriptors MIME type.

      Returns:
      :   The MIME type, which has been parsed from the
          content-type definition. Must not be null, but
          "text/plain", if no content-type was specified.

      See Also:
      :   [`getMediaType()`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/entity/mime/ContentDescriptor.html#getMediaType--),
          [`getSubType()`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/entity/mime/ContentDescriptor.html#getSubType--)
    * #### getMediaType

      ```
      String getMediaType()
      ```

      Gets the defaulted MIME media type for this content.
      For example `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `MULTIPART`

      Returns:
      :   the MIME media type when content-type specified,
          otherwise the correct default (`TEXT`)

      See Also:
      :   [`getMimeType()`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/entity/mime/ContentDescriptor.html#getMimeType--)
    * #### getSubType

      ```
      String getSubType()
      ```

      Gets the defaulted MIME sub type for this content.

      Returns:
      :   the MIME media type when content-type is specified,
          otherwise the correct default (`PLAIN`)

      See Also:
      :   [`getMimeType()`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/entity/mime/ContentDescriptor.html#getMimeType--)
    * #### getCharset

      ```
      String getCharset()
      ```

      The body descriptors character set, defaulted appropriately for the MIME type.

      For `TEXT` types, this will be defaulted to `us-ascii`.
      For other types, when the charset parameter is missing this property will be null.

      Returns:
      :   Character set, which has been parsed from the
          content-type definition. Not null for `TEXT` types, when unset will
          be set to default `us-ascii`. For other types, when unset,
          null will be returned.
    * #### getContentLength

      ```
      long getContentLength()
      ```

      Returns the body descriptors content-length.

      Returns:
      :   Content length, if known, or -1, to indicate the absence of a
          content-length header.

  * ### Method Detail

    * #### add

      ```
      public void add(String host,
                      InetAddress... ips)
      ```

      Associates the given array of IP addresses to the given host in this DNS overrider.
      The IP addresses are assumed to be already resolved.

      Parameters:
      :   `host` - The host name to be associated with the given IP.
      :   `ips` - array of IP addresses to be resolved by this DNS overrider to the given
          host name.
    * #### resolve

      ```
      public InetAddress[] resolve(String host)
                            throws UnknownHostException
      ```

      Returns the IP address for the specified host name, or null if the given
      host is not recognized or the associated IP address cannot be used to
      build an InetAddress instance.

      Specified by:
      :   `resolve` in interface `DnsResolver`

      Parameters:
      :   `host` - The host name to be resolved by this resolver.

      Returns:
      :   The IP address associated to the given host name, or null if the
          host name is not known by the implementation class.

      Throws:

## Class BackoffStrategyExec

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.BackoffStrategyExec

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [ExecChainHandler](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/classic/ExecChainHandler.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.classic")

  ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=STATELESS)
  public final class BackoffStrategyExec
  extends Object
  implements ExecChainHandler
  ```

  Request execution handler in the classic request execution chain
  that is responsible for execution of an [`ConnectionBackoffStrategy`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/classic/ConnectionBackoffStrategy.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.classic").

  Further responsibilities such as communication with the opposite
  endpoint is delegated to the next executor in the request execution
  chain.

  Since:
  :   4.3

* * ### Constructor Summary

      public ClassicHttpResponse execute(ClassicHttpRequest request,

      Description copied from interface: `ExecChainHandler`

      Executes the actual HTTP request. The handler can choose to return
      a response message or delegate request execution to the next element
      in the execution chain.

      :   `scope` - the execution scope .
      :   `chain` - the next element in the request execution chain.

      :   `HttpException`

## Class HttpRequestRetryExec

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.HttpRequestRetryExec

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [ExecChainHandler](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/classic/ExecChainHandler.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.classic")

  ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=STATELESS)
   @Internal
  public class HttpRequestRetryExec
  extends Object
  implements ExecChainHandler
  ```

  Request executor in the request execution chain that is responsible for
  making a decision whether a request that failed due to an I/O exception
  or received a specific response from the target server should
  be re-executed.

  Further responsibilities such as communication with the opposite
  endpoint is delegated to the next executor in the request execution
  chain.

  If this handler is active, pay particular attention to the placement
  of other handlers within the handler chain relative to the retry handler.
  Use [`ChainElement.RETRY`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/ChainElement.html#RETRY) as name when referring to this handler.

  If a custom handler is placed **before** the retry handler, the handler will
  see the initial request and the final outcome after the last retry. Elapsed time
  will account for any delays imposed by the retry handler.

  A custom handler which is placed **after** the retry handler will be invoked for
  each individual retry. Elapsed time will measure each individual http request,
  without the delay imposed by the retry handler.

  Since:
  :   5.0

## Interface HttpClientConnectionManager

* All Superinterfaces:
  :   [AutoCloseable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/AutoCloseable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang"), [Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.io"), [ModalCloseable](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/io/ModalCloseable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.io")

  All Known Implementing Classes:
  :   [BasicHttpClientConnectionManager](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/io/BasicHttpClientConnectionManager.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.io"), [PoolingHttpClientConnectionManager](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/io/PoolingHttpClientConnectionManager.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.io")

  ---

    

  ```
  public interface HttpClientConnectionManager
  extends ModalCloseable
  ```

  Represents a manager of persistent client connections.

  The purpose of an HTTP connection manager is to serve as a factory for new
  HTTP connections, manage persistent connections and synchronize access to
  persistent connections making sure that only one thread of execution can
  have access to a connection at a time.

  Implementations of this interface must be thread-safe. Access to shared
  data must be synchronized as methods of this interface may be executed
  from multiple threads.

  Since:
  :   4.3

* * ### Method Summary

    All Methods [Instance Methods](javascript:show(2);) [Abstract Methods](javascript:show(4);)

    | Modifier and Type | Method and Description |
    | `void` | `connect(ConnectionEndpoint endpoint, TimeValue connectTimeout, HttpContext context)` Connects the endpoint to the initial hop (connection target in case of a direct route or to the first proxy hop in case of a route via a proxy or multiple proxies). |
    | `LeaseRequest` | `lease(String id, HttpRoute route, Timeout requestTimeout, Object state)` Returns a [`LeaseRequest`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/LeaseRequest.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.io") object which can be used to obtain a [`ConnectionEndpoint`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/ConnectionEndpoint.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.io") to cancel the request by calling [`Cancellable.cancel()`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/concurrent/Cancellable.html?is-external=true#cancel-- "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.concurrent"). |
    | `void` | `release(ConnectionEndpoint endpoint, Object newState, TimeValue validDuration)` Releases the endpoint back to the manager making it potentially re-usable by other consumers. |
    | `void` | `upgrade(ConnectionEndpoint endpoint, HttpContext context)` Upgrades transport security of the given endpoint by using the TLS security protocol. |

    * ### Methods inherited from interface org.apache.hc.core5.io.[ModalCloseable](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/io/ModalCloseable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.io")

      `close`
    * ### Methods inherited from interface java.io.[Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.io")

      `close`

* * ### Method Detail

    * #### lease

      ```
      LeaseRequest lease(String id,
                         HttpRoute route,
                         Timeout requestTimeout,
                         Object state)
      ```

      Returns a [`LeaseRequest`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/LeaseRequest.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.io") object which can be used to obtain
      a [`ConnectionEndpoint`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/ConnectionEndpoint.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.io") to cancel the request by calling
      [`Cancellable.cancel()`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/concurrent/Cancellable.html?is-external=true#cancel-- "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.concurrent").

      Please note that newly allocated endpoints can be leased
      [`disconnected`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/ConnectionEndpoint.html#isConnected--). The consumer of the endpoint
      is responsible for fully establishing the route to the endpoint target
      by calling [`connect(ConnectionEndpoint, TimeValue, HttpContext)`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/HttpClientConnectionManager.html#connect-org.apache.hc.client5.http.io.ConnectionEndpoint-org.apache.hc.core5.util.TimeValue-org.apache.hc.core5.http.protocol.HttpContext-)
      in order to connect directly to the target or to the first proxy hop,
      and optionally calling [`upgrade(ConnectionEndpoint, HttpContext)`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/HttpClientConnectionManager.html#upgrade-org.apache.hc.client5.http.io.ConnectionEndpoint-org.apache.hc.core5.http.protocol.HttpContext-) method
      to upgrade the underlying transport to Transport Layer Security after having
      executed a `CONNECT` method to all intermediate proxy hops.

      Parameters:
      :   `id` - unique operation ID or `null`.
      :   `route` - HTTP route of the requested connection.
      :   `requestTimeout` - lease request timeout.
      :   `state` - expected state of the connection or `null`
          if the connection is not expected to carry any state.

      Since:
      :   5.0
    * #### release

      ```
      void release(ConnectionEndpoint endpoint,
                   Object newState,
                   TimeValue validDuration)
      ```

      Releases the endpoint back to the manager making it potentially
      re-usable by other consumers. Optionally, the maximum period
      of how long the manager should keep the connection alive can be
      defined using `validDuration` and `timeUnit`
      parameters.

      Parameters:
      :   `endpoint` - the managed endpoint.
      :   `newState` - the new connection state of `null` if state-less.
      :   `validDuration` - the duration of time this connection is valid for reuse.
    * #### connect

      ```
      void connect(ConnectionEndpoint endpoint,
                   TimeValue connectTimeout,
                   HttpContext context)
            throws IOException
      ```

      Connects the endpoint to the initial hop (connection target in case
      of a direct route or to the first proxy hop in case of a route via a proxy
      or multiple proxies).

      Parameters:
      :   `endpoint` - the managed endpoint.
      :   `connectTimeout` - connect timeout.
      :   `context` - the actual HTTP context.

      Throws:
      :   `IOException`
    * #### upgrade

      ```
      void upgrade(ConnectionEndpoint endpoint,
                   HttpContext context)
            throws IOException
      ```

      Upgrades transport security of the given endpoint by using the TLS security protocol.

      Parameters:
      :   `endpoint` - the managed endpoint.
      :   `context` - the actual HTTP context.

      Throws:
      :   `IOException`

## Class IdleConnectionEvictor

  ```
  @Contract(threading=SAFE_CONDITIONAL)
  public final class IdleConnectionEvictor
  extends Object
  ```

  This class maintains a background thread to enforce an eviction policy for expired / idle
  persistent connections kept alive in the connection pool.

## Class ContentCodecRegistry

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity.compress.ContentCodecRegistry

* ---

    

  ```
  @Internal
   @Contract(threading=STATELESS)
  public final class ContentCodecRegistry
  extends Object
  ```

  Registry of encode/decode transformations for HTTP content codings.

  Entries are wired once at class-load time and exposed via an unmodifiable map.
  Built-in gzip/deflate are always available. Additional codecs are discovered
  reflectively:

  * Commons Compress codecs, when the library and (if required) its helper JARs
    are present.
  * Decode-only Brotli via brotli4j, when present on the classpath. This does
    not affect the advertised `Accept-Encoding` unless an encoder is also
    registered.

  Since:
  :   5.6

  ---

    

  ```
  public interface BackoffManager
  ```

  Represents a controller that dynamically adjusts the size
  of an available connection pool based on feedback from
  using the connections.

  Since:
  :   4.2

* * ### Method Summary

    All Methods [Instance Methods](javascript:show(2);) [Abstract Methods](javascript:show(4);)

    | Modifier and Type | Method and Description |
    | `void` | `backOff(HttpRoute route)` Called when we have decided that the result of using a connection should be interpreted as a backoff signal. |
    | `void` | `probe(HttpRoute route)` Called when we have determined that the result of using a connection has succeeded and that we may probe for more connections. |

* * ### Method Detail

org.apache.hc.client5.http.async

## Interface AsyncExecCallback

* ---

    

  ```
  public interface AsyncExecCallback
  ```

  AsyncExecCallback methods represent response processing events
  in the client side request execution chain.

  Since:
  :   5.0

* * ### Method Summary

    All Methods [Instance Methods](javascript:show(2);) [Abstract Methods](javascript:show(4);)

    | Modifier and Type | Method and Description |
    | `void` | `completed()` Triggered to signal completion of the message exchange. |
    | `void` | `failed(Exception cause)` Triggered to signal a failure occurred during the message exchange. |
    | `void` | `handleInformationResponse(HttpResponse response)` Triggered to signal receipt of an intermediate response message. |
    | `AsyncDataConsumer` | `handleResponse(HttpResponse response, EntityDetails entityDetails)` Triggered to signal receipt of a response message head sent by the server in response to the request being executed. |

* * ### Method Detail

    * #### handleResponse

      ```
      AsyncDataConsumer handleResponse(HttpResponse response,
                                       EntityDetails entityDetails)
                                throws HttpException,
                                       IOException
      ```

      Triggered to signal receipt of a response message head sent by the server
      in response to the request being executed.

      Parameters:
      :   `response` - the response message head.
      :   `entityDetails` - the response entity details or `null` if the response
          does not enclose an entity.

      Returns:
      :   the data consumer to be used for processing of incoming response message body.

      Throws:
      :   `HttpException` - If a protocol error occurs.
      :   `IOException` - If an I/O error occurs.
    * #### handleInformationResponse

      ```
      void handleInformationResponse(HttpResponse response)
                              throws HttpException,
                                     IOException
      ```

      Triggered to signal receipt of an intermediate response message.

      Parameters:
      :   `response` - the intermediate response message.

      Throws:
      :   `HttpException` - If a protocol error occurs.
      :   `IOException` - If an I/O error occurs.
    * #### completed

      ```
      void completed()
      ```

      Triggered to signal completion of the message exchange.

      Implementations of this message are expected to perform resource deallocation
      allocated in the course of the request execution and response processing.
    * #### failed

      ```
      void failed(Exception cause)
      ```

      Triggered to signal a failure occurred during the message exchange.

      Implementations of this message are expected to perform resource deallocation
      allocated in the course of the request execution and response processing.

  [`CookieSpecFactory`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/cookie/CookieSpecFactory.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.cookie") implementation that provides an instance of

  can be shared by multiple threads.

## Class PublicSuffixList

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * org.apache.hc.client5.http.psl.PublicSuffixList

* ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=IMMUTABLE)
  public final class PublicSuffixList
  extends Object
  ```

  Public suffix is a set of DNS names or wildcards concatenated with dots. It represents
  the part of a domain name which is not under the control of the individual registrant

  An up-to-date list of suffixes can be obtained from
  [publicsuffix.org](http://publicsuffix.org/)

  Since:
  :   4.4

## Class ExponentialBackoffManager

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * [org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.AbstractBackoff](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/AbstractBackoff.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic")
  * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.ExponentialBackoffManager

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [BackoffManager](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/classic/BackoffManager.html "interface in org.apache.hc.client5.http.classic")

  ---

    

  ```
  public class ExponentialBackoffManager
  extends AbstractBackoff
  ```

  A backoff manager implementation that uses an exponential backoff algorithm to adjust the maximum
  number of connections per HTTP route. The algorithm reduces the number of connections in response
  to adverse events, such as connection failures, and gradually increases the number of connections
  when the route is operating without issues.

  This implementation is specifically designed for managing connections in an HTTP route context
  and provides methods for probing and backing off connections based on the performance of the route.

  The exponential backoff algorithm is primarily implemented in the `getBackedOffPoolSize`
  method, which calculates the new connection pool size based on the current pool size, growth rate,
  and the number of time intervals.

  Since:
  :   5.3

    | `ExponentialBackoffManager(ConnPoolControl<HttpRoute> connPerRoute)` Constructs a new ExponentialBackoffManager with the specified connection pool control. |

    * ### Methods inherited from class org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic.[AbstractBackoff](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/AbstractBackoff.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.classic")

      `clone, equals, finalize, getClass, hashCode, notify, notifyAll, toString, wait, wait, wait`

* * ### Constructor Detail

    * #### ExponentialBackoffManager

      ```
      public ExponentialBackoffManager(ConnPoolControl<HttpRoute> connPerRoute)
      ```

      Constructs a new ExponentialBackoffManager with the specified connection pool control.

      Parameters:
      :   `connPerRoute` - the connection pool control to be used for managing connections

      Throws:
      :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if connPerRoute is null
  * ### Method Detail

    * #### getBackedOffPoolSize

      ```
      protected int getBackedOffPoolSize(int curr)
      ```

      Calculates the new pool size after applying the exponential backoff algorithm.
      The new pool size is calculated using the formula: floor(curr / (1 + growthRate) ^ t),
      where curr is the current pool size, growthRate is the exponential growth rate, and t is the time interval.

      Specified by:
      :   `getBackedOffPoolSize` in class `AbstractBackoff`

      Parameters:
      :   `curr` - the current pool size

      Returns:
      :   the new pool size after applying the backoff
    * #### setBackoffFactor

      ```
      public void setBackoffFactor(double rate)
      ```

      Description copied from class: `AbstractBackoff`

      Sets the backoff factor for the backoff algorithm.
      The backoff factor should be a value between 0.0 and 1.0.
      The specific implementation of how the backoff factor is used should be provided by subclasses.

      Parameters:
      :   `rate` - the backoff factor to be set

## Interface AsyncExecChainHandler

* All Known Implementing Classes:
  :   [AsyncConnectExec](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/AsyncConnectExec.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.async"), [AsyncHttpRequestRetryExec](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/AsyncHttpRequestRetryExec.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.async"), [AsyncProtocolExec](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/AsyncProtocolExec.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.async"), [AsyncRedirectExec](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/AsyncRedirectExec.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.async"), [ContentCompressionAsyncExec](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/ContentCompressionAsyncExec.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.async"), [EarlyHintsAsyncExec](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/EarlyHintsAsyncExec.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.async"), [H2AsyncMainClientExec](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/H2AsyncMainClientExec.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.async")

  ---

    

  ```
  @Contract(threading=STATELESS)
  public interface AsyncExecChainHandler
  ```

  Abstract request execution handler in an asynchronous client side request execution
  chain. Handlers can either be a decorator around another element that implements
  a cross cutting aspect or a self-contained executor capable of producing a response
  for the given request.

  For information regarding the handler chain behaviour in case of a request re-execution,
  please refer to the [`AsyncHttpRequestRetryExec`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/AsyncHttpRequestRetryExec.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.async") javadoc.

  Well known request execution handlers could be referred to by name using one of the
  [`ChainElement`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/ChainElement.html "enum in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl") enum values.

  Since:
  :   5.0

  See Also:
  :   [`ChainElement`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/ChainElement.html "enum in org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl"),
      [`HttpAsyncClientBuilder.addExecInterceptorFirst(String, AsyncExecChainHandler)`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/HttpAsyncClientBuilder.html#addExecInterceptorFirst-java.lang.String-org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.AsyncExecChainHandler-),
      [`HttpAsyncClientBuilder.addExecInterceptorBefore(String, String, AsyncExecChainHandler)`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/HttpAsyncClientBuilder.html#addExecInterceptorBefore-java.lang.String-java.lang.String-org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.AsyncExecChainHandler-),
      [`HttpAsyncClientBuilder.addExecInterceptorAfter(String, String, AsyncExecChainHandler)`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/HttpAsyncClientBuilder.html#addExecInterceptorAfter-java.lang.String-java.lang.String-org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.AsyncExecChainHandler-),
      [`HttpAsyncClientBuilder.addExecInterceptorLast(String, AsyncExecChainHandler)`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/HttpAsyncClientBuilder.html#addExecInterceptorLast-java.lang.String-org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.AsyncExecChainHandler-)

* * ### Method Summary

    All Methods [Instance Methods](javascript:show(2);) [Abstract Methods](javascript:show(4);)

    | Modifier and Type | Method and Description |
    | `void` | `execute(HttpRequest request, AsyncEntityProducer entityProducer, AsyncExecChain.Scope scope, AsyncExecChain chain, AsyncExecCallback asyncExecCallback)` Executes the actual HTTP request. |

* * ### Method Detail

    * #### execute

      ```
      void execute(HttpRequest request,
                   AsyncEntityProducer entityProducer,
                   AsyncExecChain.Scope scope,
                   AsyncExecChain chain,
                   AsyncExecCallback asyncExecCallback)
            throws HttpException,
                   IOException
      ```

      Executes the actual HTTP request. The handler can choose to return
      a response message immediately inside the call or asynchronously
      at some later point or delegate request execution to the next
      element in the execution chain.

      Parameters:
      :   `request` - the actual request.
      :   `entityProducer` - the request entity producer or `null` if the request
          does not enclose an entity.
      :   `scope` - the execution scope .
      :   `chain` - the next element in the request execution chain.
      :   `asyncExecCallback` - the execution callback.

      Throws:
      :   `HttpException` - If a protocol error occurs.
      :   `IOException` - If an I/O error occurs.

## Class ZstdRuntime

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.ZstdRuntime

* ---

    

  ```
  @Internal
   @Contract(threading=STATELESS)
  public final class ZstdRuntime
  extends Object
  ```

  Utility to detect availability of the Zstandard JNI runtime on the classpath.

  Used by the async client implementation to *conditionally* register
  zstd encoders/decoders without creating a hard dependency on `zstd-jni`.

  This class performs a lightweight reflective check and intentionally avoids
  linking to JNI classes at compile time to prevent [`LinkageError`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/LinkageError.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")s when
  the optional dependency is absent.

  Since:
  :   5.6

* * ### Method Summary

    All Methods [Static Methods](javascript:show(1);) [Concrete Methods](javascript:show(8);)

    | Modifier and Type | Method and Description |
    | `static boolean` | `available()` |

    * ### Methods inherited from class java.lang.[Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")

* * ### Method Detail

      public static boolean available()
      ```

      :   `true` if `com.github.luben.zstd.Zstd` can be loaded
          by the current class loader; `false` otherwise

## Class SimpleRequestBuilder

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * [org.apache.hc.core5.http.support.AbstractMessageBuilder](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/support/AbstractMessageBuilder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.support")<T>
  * * [org.apache.hc.core5.http.support.AbstractRequestBuilder](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/support/AbstractRequestBuilder.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.support")<[SimpleHttpRequest](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/async/methods/SimpleHttpRequest.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods")>
    * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods.SimpleRequestBuilder

* ---

    

  ```
  public class SimpleRequestBuilder
  extends AbstractRequestBuilder<SimpleHttpRequest>
  ```

  Builder for [`SimpleHttpRequest`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/async/methods/SimpleHttpRequest.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods") instances.

  Please note that this class treats parameters differently depending on composition
  of the request: if the request has a content entity explicitly set with
  [`setBody(SimpleBody)`](../../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/async/methods/SimpleRequestBuilder.html#setBody-org.apache.hc.client5.http.async.methods.SimpleBody-) or it is not an entity enclosing method
  (such as POST or PUT), parameters will be added to the query component
  of the request URI. Otherwise, parameters will be added as a URL encoded entity.

  Since:
  :   5.0

## Class CompressingEntity

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * [org.apache.hc.core5.http.io.entity.HttpEntityWrapper](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/io/entity/HttpEntityWrapper.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.io.entity")
  * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity.compress.CompressingEntity

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.io"), [AutoCloseable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/AutoCloseable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang"), [EntityDetails](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/EntityDetails.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http"), [HttpEntity](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/HttpEntity.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http")

  ---

    

  ```
  public final class CompressingEntity
  extends HttpEntityWrapper
  ```

  Streaming wrapper that compresses the enclosed [`HttpEntity`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/HttpEntity.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http") on write.

  The actual compressor is supplied as an [`IOFunction`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/io/IOFunction.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.io")<OutputStream,OutputStream>
  and is resolved by the caller (for example via reflective factories). This keeps
  compression back-ends fully optional and avoids hard classpath dependencies.

  The entity reports the configured `Content-Encoding` token and streams
  the content; length is unknown (`-1`), and the entity is chunked.

  Since:
  :   5.6

## Class DeflateDecompressingEntity

* [java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang")
* * [org.apache.hc.core5.http.io.entity.HttpEntityWrapper](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/io/entity/HttpEntityWrapper.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.io.entity")
  * * [org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity.DecompressingEntity](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/entity/DecompressingEntity.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity")
    * * org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity.DeflateDecompressingEntity

* All Implemented Interfaces:
  :   [Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.io"), [AutoCloseable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/AutoCloseable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang"), [EntityDetails](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/EntityDetails.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http"), [HttpEntity](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/HttpEntity.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http")

  ---

  Deprecated.

  See [`ContentCodecRegistry.decoder(org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity.compress.ContentCoding)`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/entity/compress/ContentCodecRegistry.html#decoder-org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity.compress.ContentCoding-)

    

  ```
  @Deprecated
  public class DeflateDecompressingEntity
  extends DecompressingEntity
  ```

  [`HttpEntityWrapper`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/http/io/entity/HttpEntityWrapper.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.http.io.entity") responsible for
  handling deflate Content Coded responses. In RFC2616 terms, `deflate`
  means a `zlib` stream as defined in RFC1950. Some server
  implementations have misinterpreted RFC2616 to mean that a
  `deflate` stream as defined in RFC1951 should be used
  (or maybe they did that since that's how IE behaves?). It's confusing
  that `deflate` in HTTP 1.1 means `zlib` streams
  rather than `deflate` streams. We handle both types in here,
  since that's what is seen on the internet. Moral - prefer
  `gzip`!

  Since:
  :   4.1

  See Also:
  :   [`GzipDecompressingEntity`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/entity/GzipDecompressingEntity.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.entity")

## Interface LeaseRequest

* All Superinterfaces:
  :   [Cancellable](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/concurrent/Cancellable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.concurrent")

  ---

    

  ```
  public interface LeaseRequest
  extends Cancellable
  ```

  Represents a request for a [`ConnectionEndpoint`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/ConnectionEndpoint.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.io") whose life cycle
  is managed by a connection manager.

  Since:
  :   5.0

* * ### Method Summary

    All Methods [Instance Methods](javascript:show(2);) [Abstract Methods](javascript:show(4);)

    | Modifier and Type | Method and Description |
    | `ConnectionEndpoint` | `get(Timeout timeout)` Returns [`ConnectionEndpoint`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/ConnectionEndpoint.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.io") within a given time. |

    * ### Methods inherited from interface org.apache.hc.core5.concurrent.[Cancellable](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/concurrent/Cancellable.html?is-external=true "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.concurrent")

      `cancel`

* * ### Method Detail

    * #### get

      ```
      ConnectionEndpoint get(Timeout timeout)
                      throws InterruptedException,
                             ExecutionException,
                             TimeoutException
      ```

      Returns [`ConnectionEndpoint`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/io/ConnectionEndpoint.html "class in org.apache.hc.client5.http.io") within a given time.
      This method will block until a connection becomes available,
      the timeout expires, or the connection manager is shut down.
      Timeouts are handled with millisecond precision.
      If [`Cancellable.cancel()`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-5.4.x/current/httpcore5/apidocs/org/apache/hc/core5/concurrent/Cancellable.html?is-external=true#cancel-- "class or interface in org.apache.hc.core5.concurrent") is called while this is blocking or
      before this began, an [`InterruptedException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/InterruptedException.html?is-external=true "class or interface in java.lang") will
      be thrown.

      Parameters:
      :   `timeout` - the operation timeout.

      Returns:
      :   a connection that can be used to communicate
          along the given route

      Throws:
      :   `TimeoutException` - in case of a timeout
      :   `InterruptedException` - if the calling thread is interrupted while waiting
      :   `ExecutionException`

      :   `host` - target host as specified by the caller (end user).
      :   `remoteAddress` - the resolved remote address to connect to.
      :   `localAddress` - the local address to bind the socket to, or `null` for any.
      :   `context` - the actual HTTP context.

      Returns:
      :   the connected socket. The returned object may be different
          from the `sock` argument if this factory supports
          a layered protocol.

      Throws:
      :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs
    * #### connectSocket

      ```

                                   HttpHost host,
                                   InetSocketAddress remoteAddress,
                                   InetSocketAddress localAddress,
                                   Timeout connectTimeout,
                                   Object attachment,
                                   HttpContext context)
                            throws IOException
      ```

      Deprecated.

      Connects the socket to the target host with the given resolved remote address.

      Parameters:
      :   `socket` - the socket to connect, as obtained from [`createSocket(HttpContext)`](../../../../../../org/apache/hc/client5/http/socket/ConnectionSocketFactory.html#createSocket-org.apache.hc.core5.http.protocol.HttpContext-).
          `null` indicates that a new socket should be created and connected.
      :   `host` - target host as specified by the caller (end user).
      :   `remoteAddress` - the resolved remote address to connect to.
      :   `localAddress` - the local address to bind the socket to, or `null` for any.
      :   `connectTimeout` - connect timeout.
      :   `attachment` - connect request attachment.
      :   `context` - the actual HTTP context.

      Returns:
      :   the connected socket. The returned object may be different
          from the `sock` argument if this factory supports
          a layered protocol.

      Throws:
      :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs

      Since:
